claims.explanation: SC-9 is a naphthalenesulfonamide PKC activator that kills cells dependent on PKC signaling, and the selective pattern is best explained by TP53 loss combined with intact PKC pathway activity. TP53-mutant lines are enriched among sensitive lines, while resistant lines frequently retain wild-type TP53 or have alterations that blunt PKC-driven growth inhibition, such as SMARCA4 loss or NRAS activation. PRKCA expression and PKC-pathway activity are predicted to sensitize, whereas mutations in NRAS, SMARCA4, and ARID1A are protective.

features.basis: TP53 mutations are highly enriched in the most-killed lines and rare in the least-affected lines
SC-9 activates PKC and PRKCA is the annotated target; higher expression should increase drug effect
NRAS-mutant lines (NCIH1299, IPC298, KU1919, SKNSH) are overrepresented among least-affected lines
SMARCA4-mutant lines (COV434, NCIH841, NCIH1573, SKNSH) appear among least-affected lines
ARID1A mutations occur in several least-affected lines (COLO792, KU1919, HS766T) and are absent from the sensitive set
CDKN2A loss co-occurs with TP53 mutation in many sensitive lines and may enhance PKC-driven growth inhibition
KRAS-mutant lines are common among least-affected lines (SW480, LS1034, NCIH1573, HS766T)
BRAF-mutant melanomas UACC62 and G361 are among the most-killed lines
PTEN loss in UACC62 and U118MG may alter PKC/PI3K crosstalk, though U118MG is resistant
ATM mutations appear in several least-affected lines (SNU685, OV90) and in some sensitive lines, weakening the signal
NF1 mutations appear in several sensitive lines (RD, MDAMB361, YD8) but also in resistant COLO792
ALK mutations occur in resistant neuroblastoma lines KELLY and SKNSH
